title: Karen Insurgency Escalates, Burma Faces Multi-Front Rebellions
note: The KNU capture of Insein and the siege there occurred in January-May 1949, not 1950. The 111-day Battle of Insein ended 22 May 1949. The year is off by one. The multi-front framing (CPB + KMT + KNU) is accurate for 1950 context, but the Insein capture cited in the description is a 1949 event.

title: KMT Remnants Occupy Shan State, Forcing UN Intervention
note: Confirmed: KMT 8th Army (Li Mi) crossed into Shan State from Yunnan in late 1949/early 1950; CIA backing confirmed; Burma raised matter at UN; ~1,500 initial soldiers figure is consistent with sources (grew later). UN passed resolution demanding withdrawal. Year, actors, and core claim all verified.

title: Burma Holds First Post-Independence General Elections
note: Confirmed: elections held June 1951-April 1952 (phased). AFPFL won 199/250 seats. Turnout only 20% (1.5M of 8M eligible). U Nu confirmed as PM. Low turnout in insurgency-affected areas noted. Year 1951 is accurate for election start.

title: Burma-China Border Demarcation Talks Begin
note: Confirmed: Zhou Enlai visited Burma in 1954 and issued Joint Declaration on Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence; formal border demarcation talks began then. Final border treaty signed 1 October 1960. Year, actors, and outcome match.

title: Nationalization of Key Industries Under Socialist Program
note: Confirmed: AFPFL government accelerated nationalization of rice mills, timber, and oil from the early 1950s through the decade. British and Indian commercial interests were bought out. Decline of rice exports is documented. Year is a reasonable attribution for a multi-year process.

title: Ne Win Caretaker Government Takes Power Amid AFPFL Crisis
note: Confirmed: Ne Win became interim PM on 28 October 1958 after AFPFL split into Clean (U Nu) and Stable (Ba Swe/Kyaw Nyein) factions. U Nu invited Ne Win after barely surviving a no-confidence vote. Power restored to U Nu after February 1960 elections.

title: Buddhism Declared State Religion, Alarming Ethnic Minorities
note: Confirmed: Parliament passed Third Amendment to the Constitution on 26 August 1961 making Buddhism the state religion. Protests from Karen, Kachin, Chin minorities documented. Military later cited this as justification for 1962 coup. Year and actors match.

title: Ne Win Military Coup Overthrows Parliamentary Democracy
note: Confirmed: Ne Win led predawn coup on 2 March 1962. U Nu and ethnic Shan leaders attending federal seminar arrested. Revolutionary Council declared martial law, dissolved Parliament. Date, actors, and framing all verified.

title: Rangoon University Student Union Demolished, Students Killed
note: Confirmed: Protests on 7 July 1962; soldiers fired on students (official count 16 killed, eyewitnesses say 100+). RUSU building demolished with dynamite on morning of 8 July 1962. Description accurately characterizes it as July 1962.

title: Burmese Way to Socialism and Mass Nationalization Proclaimed
note: Confirmed: Enterprise Nationalization Law passed 1 June 1963, nationalizing all major industries including import-export, rice, banking, teak. By mid-1963, 2,500 foreigners/week leaving; ~100,000 Indians emigrated by 1964. The philosophical manifesto was published January 1963. Year and facts match.

title: Failed Peace Talks with Ethnic Armed Groups
note: Confirmed: Ne Win held peace talks with insurgent groups in 1963-64. They failed because Ne Win refused federalism ('Federalism is impossible'). Both CPB and ethnic groups returned to armed struggle. Year range 1963-64 matches description.

title: Anti-Chinese Riots and Diplomatic Rupture with Beijing
note: Confirmed: Anti-Chinese riots erupted 26 June 1967 in Rangoon, triggered by Chinese students wearing Mao badges. 31 Chinese killed, dozens of Chinese businesses attacked. China suspended diplomatic relations and redirected support to CPB. Year and core facts verified.

title: Communist Party of Burma Launches Chinese-Backed Northern Offensive
note: Confirmed: CPB forces crossed from Yunnan into Shan State on 1 January 1968, taking Kokang region. Chinese weapons and training confirmed. Established base area along Chinese border. Year and core facts match.

title: Socialist Constitution Enacted Amid Worker Strikes
note: Confirmed: 1974 constitution promulgated 3 January 1974. Worker strikes at state enterprises in May-June 1974 (Thamaing Textile Factory workers killed). U Thant funeral protest in December 1974, students seized coffin, military stormed Rangoon University 11 December 1974. Both episodes correctly dated.

title: National Democratic Front Formed by Ethnic Armed Organizations
note: Confirmed: Federal National Democratic Front formed 1975, renamed National Democratic Front (NDF) in May 1976. Included KNU, KIO, and Shan groups. Founded at KNU base on Thai border. Ten groups confirmed. Year slightly nuanced (formal NDF name from 1976) but founding date of 1975 is accurate.

title: Operation Nagamin Drives 200,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh
note: Confirmed: Operation Nagamin (also known as Operation Dragon King) began 6 February 1978 in northern Arakan. By May 1978, 200,000-250,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh. UNHCR brokered repatriation; 180,000 returned. Year and refugee count match.

title: Citizenship Law Renders Rohingya Stateless by Statute
note: Confirmed: 1982 Burma Citizenship Law defines citizenship through 135 national races present before 1823 British annexation. Rohingya explicitly excluded, rendered stateless in law. International legal scholars have described it as structural statelessness. Year and core facts fully verified.

title: North Korean Bombing of South Korean Officials in Rangoon
note: Confirmed: Bombing at Martyrs Mausoleum on 9 October 1983. Three North Korean agents planted bombs. 21 people killed (4 were Burmese); South Korean President Chun Doo-hwan survived as his car was late. Burma arrested the agents, tried them, and severed diplomatic relations with North Korea. Year and facts match. Note: description says 17 South Korean + 4 Burmese = 21 total, which is correct; description incorrectly states '17 South Korean and four Burmese officials killed'—actual toll was 21 total (not all officials).

title: Least Developed Country Status Accepted After Decades of Mismanagement
note: Year error: Burma was accepted onto the LDC list in 1987, not 1985. The 1985 demonetization of 100 and 50 kyat notes is also misattributed — the actual demonetization destroying savings was in September 1987 (25, 35, 75 kyat notes). The event conflates 1985 and 1987 dates incorrectly.

title: Logging Concessions Drive Mass Deforestation Along Thai Border
note: Year error: The documented SLORC logging deals with 42 Thai companies were struck in 1989, not 1986. The SLORC took power in September 1988; the logging concessions were a post-SLORC phenomenon. The event is real but misattributed to 1986.

title: 1987 Demonetization Wipes Out Savings, Triggers Popular Rage
note: Confirmed: On 5 September 1987, Ne Win announced demonetization of 25, 35, and 75 kyat notes, wiping out ~80% of currency in circulation. Denominations chosen by numerology (multiples of 9). Directly triggered 1988 uprising. Year and facts match.

title: 8888 Uprising — Mass Democracy Movement Across Burma
note: Confirmed: 8-8-88 nationwide general strike on 8 August 1988. Millions mobilized — students, monks, workers, doctors. Military fired on protesters; estimated 3,000-10,000 killed. Ended with SLORC coup 18 September 1988. All core facts verified.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Emerges as Opposition Leader
note: Confirmed: Suu Kyi returned to Burma in 1988 to nurse ailing mother. Delivered Shwedagon Pagoda speech on 26 August 1988 to ~500,000 people. Co-founded NLD on 27 September 1988 (with former General Tin Oo). Year, date, and facts verified.

title: SLORC Coup Ends Socialist Era, Establishes New Junta
note: Confirmed: General Saw Maung led coup on 18 September 1988, established SLORC. Ne Win formally stepped down as BSPP chairman. Martial law declared, Parliament dissolved. Date, actor, and facts verified.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Placed Under First House Arrest
note: Confirmed: Suu Kyi placed under house arrest on 20 July 1989 under emergency security laws. Pattern of confinement totaling ~15 years across three periods is accurate. Year and core facts verified.

title: Communist Party of Burma Collapses, UWSA Emerges
note: Confirmed: Ethnic Wa soldiers mutinied against Burman CPB leadership in April 1989, seizing HQ at Panghsang on 17 April 1989. UWSA formed and signed ceasefire with Myanmar government 9 May 1989. China acquiesced. UWSA became one of Southeast Asia's largest armed forces. Year and facts verified.

title: 1990 Elections Won by NLD in Landslide, SLORC Refuses Transfer of Power
note: Confirmed: NLD won 392 of 485 seats (80.82%) in 27 May 1990 elections. SLORC refused power transfer, claiming elections were only to select constitutional convention members. International outrage ensued. Event description notes 392 of 492 seats — actual contested seats were 485 (NLD won 392). Minor count discrepancy but core facts verified.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Awarded Nobel Peace Prize While Under House Arrest
note: Confirmed: Nobel Peace Prize 1991 awarded to Suu Kyi. Her son Alexander Aris (and husband Michael Aris) accepted on her behalf at Oslo ceremony 10 December 1991. Prize money (~$1.3M USD) established health and education trust. Year and facts verified.

title: Second Rohingya Mass Exodus — 250,000 Flee to Bangladesh
note: Confirmed: Operation Pyi Thaya (Clean and Beautiful Nation) from December 1991 to March 1992 drove 210,000-250,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. UNHCR brokered repatriation. Year and scale match.

title: Ceasefire Agreements with Ethnic Armed Groups
note: Confirmed: SLORC negotiated ceasefire agreements with ethnic armed groups from 1989 onward; approximately 15-17 groups by mid-1990s (UWSA 1989, KIO 1994, NMSP 1995, others). Logging and mining concessions offered in exchange. Fundamental political questions left unresolved. Year 1993 is appropriate as the mid-range of the process.

title: Yadana Gas Pipeline — Largest Foreign Investment, Forced Labor Documented
note: Confirmed: Yadana pipeline project involved Total S.A. and Unocal (US) connecting Andaman Sea gas to Thailand. Forced labor documented by Unocal's own consultant in 1995. Doe v. Unocal lawsuit filed 1996, settled 2005. Pipeline revenues went to military. Year 1994 accurate for project commencement.

title: Fall of Karen HQ Manerplaw to Burmese Army
note: Confirmed: Manerplaw fell on 27 January 1995 to Tatmadaw and DKBA (Buddhist Karen splinter). ~10,000 refugees fled to Thailand across Moei River. Democratic Alliance of Burma coalition dissolved. Year and facts verified.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Released from First Period of House Arrest
note: Confirmed: Released 10 July 1995 after six years of house arrest. Resumed political activity. NLD reappointed her general secretary 10 October 1995. Year and facts verified.

title: Large Student Protests Suppressed in Rangoon
note: Confirmed: Student protests in December 1996, largest since 1988. Demands for independent student union and end to police brutality. Riot police dispersed protesters; universities closed. Some activists fled to border areas. Year and facts match.

title: Myanmar Joins ASEAN Despite International Protest
note: Confirmed: Myanmar formally admitted to ASEAN on 23 July 1997 at ceremony in Subang Jaya, Malaysia. US and EU objected citing human rights violations. ASEAN's non-interference principle invoked. Concurrent Asian financial crisis accurate. Year and facts verified.

title: Drug Warlord Khun Sa Surrenders to Myanmar Government
note: Year error: Khun Sa surrendered to Myanmar military government on 5 January 1996, not 1999. He lived in Yangon seclusion from 1996 until his death in October 2007. The event is real but dated three years too late.

title: US and European Sanctions Tightened on Myanmar Junta
note: Confirmed: US and EU maintained and periodically tightened sanctions through early 2000s including visa bans, asset freezes, import restrictions. Myanmar relied on China, Thailand, India as economic lifelines. Year 2001 is a reasonable attribution for a sustained process.

title: Buddhist-Muslim Communal Violence Erupts in Central Myanmar
note: Confirmed: Communal violence between Buddhists and Muslims in several central Myanmar towns in 2001. Mosques and Muslim-owned businesses attacked. Security forces accused of passivity. Foreshadowed later systematic violence. Year and core facts consistent with documented incidents.

title: Depayin Massacre of NLD Convoy
note: Confirmed: Depayin massacre on 30 May 2003. USDA/government-organized mob of ~5,000 ambushed NLD convoy. At least 70 NLD supporters killed (some estimates 100+). Suu Kyi narrowly escaped, subsequently re-arrested. No perpetrators prosecuted. All core facts verified.

title: Seven-Step Roadmap to Discipline-Flourishing Democracy Announced
note: Confirmed: PM Khin Nyunt announced seven-step roadmap in August 2003. Presented as transition plan, dismissed internationally as a delaying mechanism. Structured Myanmar's constitutional process on military's terms through 2008 constitution and 2010 elections. Year and characterization verified.

title: Khin Nyunt Purged, Military Intelligence Dissolved
note: Confirmed: Khin Nyunt 'permitted to retire' on 18 October 2004 (immediately arrested). Military Intelligence Directorate comprehensively purged and replaced by Office of the Chief of Military Security Affairs. Than Shwe eliminated main internal pragmatist. Year and facts verified.

title: Capital Relocated to Purpose-Built Naypyidaw
note: Confirmed: Capital officially moved on 6 November 2005 (convoy arrived 11 November 2005). Sudden relocation without public consultation. Astrologers cited in multiple sources. Official name Naypyidaw revealed 27 March 2006 (Armed Forces Day). Year verified.

title: ILO Documents Systematic Forced Labor by Myanmar Military
note: Confirmed: ILO documented widespread forced labor by Myanmar military throughout 2000s in rural areas. ILO complaints mechanism established. Forced labor endemic and rooted in pre-colonial corvee traditions. Year 2006 is a reasonable attribution for ongoing documented practice.

title: Saffron Revolution — Monk-Led Protests and Violent Crackdown
note: Confirmed: Protests started 19 August 2007 after 15 August fuel price increase (up to 500%). Monks led mass demonstrations. Crackdown 25-27 September 2007. Over 6,000 arrested. Japanese journalist Kenji Nagai shot dead 27 September 2007. Death toll 13-31 confirmed dead. All core facts verified.

title: Cyclone Nargis Kills Over 130,000 — Junta Blocks Aid
note: Confirmed: Cyclone Nargis struck 2-3 May 2008. Official figures: 84,537 confirmed dead + 53,800 missing = ~138,000 total. Some estimates exceed 138,373 fatalities. SPDC blocked foreign aid workers for critical weeks. ASEAN brokered eventual access. Year and facts verified.

title: 2008 Constitution Approved, Institutionalizes Military Veto
note: Confirmed: Referendum held 10 May 2008, one week after Cyclone Nargis. Officially 92.48% approval (widely dismissed as fabricated). 25% of parliamentary seats reserved for military appointees. Supermajority required to amend key provisions. Foreign-spouse bar targeting Suu Kyi confirmed. Year and facts verified.

title: 2010 Elections Held Under Flawed Rules, NLD Boycotts, Suu Kyi Released
note: Confirmed: Elections held November 2010. NLD boycotted because election law required expelling Suu Kyi as condition for registration. USDP (military proxy) won large majority. Suu Kyi released 13 November 2010 (six days after vote, not 'six days after' but the description captures this accurately). Year and facts verified.

title: Thein Sein Launches Genuine Reform Program
note: Confirmed: Thein Sein released 200+ political prisoners, relaxed censorship, entered dialogue with Suu Kyi, suspended Myitsone Dam in September 2011. Clinton visited Yangon. Western sanctions eased. Year and facts verified.

title: Kachin War Resumes After 17-Year Ceasefire
note: Confirmed: Armed clashes erupted on 9 June 2011 when government forces attacked KIA positions along Taping River. KIA refused to transform into Border Guard Force. 17-year ceasefire broken (from 1994). Over 100,000 IDPs created. Year and date verified.

title: NLD Wins By-Elections, Aung San Suu Kyi Enters Parliament
note: Confirmed: NLD won 43 of 45 seats in 1 April 2012 by-elections. Suu Kyi won Kawhmu constituency with ~99% of votes. She entered parliament for first time. Internationally assessed as genuinely free and fair. Year and facts verified.

title: Rakhine State Violence Displaces 140,000 Rohingya into Camps
note: Confirmed: Communal violence in June and October 2012. ~140,000 Rohingya displaced into camps (37 camps across Rakhine). Government figures: 167 killed. Security forces accused of participating in or standing by during attacks. Year and displacement figure verified.

title: Race and Religion Protection Laws Codify Discrimination
note: Year error: The four Race and Religion Protection Laws were submitted to Parliament in December 2014 but adopted/signed into law in 2015 (Interfaith Marriage Law and Religious Conversion Law signed 26 May 2015; others passed in spring 2015). The event should be attributed to 2015, not 2014. The promotion campaign by Ma Ba Tha was indeed 2014 but legal enactment was 2015.

title: Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement Signed with Eight Ethnic Groups
note: Confirmed: Eight ethnic armed organizations signed NCA on 15 October 2015. Major groups including KIO, UWSA declined. Covered less than half of actual armed actors. Year and facts verified.

title: NLD Wins Landslide Election, Historic Democratic Transition Begins
note: Confirmed: NLD won 255 of 330 elected lower house seats in 8 November 2015 elections. Suu Kyi appointed State Counsellor 6 April 2016 (new position circumventing presidential bar). 50 years of military executive control ended. Year and facts verified.

title: ARSA Attacks on Border Posts Trigger Military Crackdown in Rakhine
note: Confirmed: ARSA (then Harakah al-Yaqin) attacked border police posts on 9 October 2016, killing nine officers in Maungdaw Township. Military crackdown followed with documented atrocities against Rohingya civilians. ~87,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh. Year and facts verified.

title: Rohingya Genocide — Military Offensive Drives 700,000 into Bangladesh
note: Confirmed: ARSA attacks on 25 August 2017 triggered military clearance operation. UN Fact-Finding Mission characterized it as genocide and crimes against humanity. Over 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh within weeks. Cox's Bazar became world's largest refugee camp complex. ICJ proceedings initiated. All core facts verified.

title: Reuters Journalists Imprisoned for Rohingya Massacre Reporting
note: Confirmed: Wa Lone and Kyaw Soe Oo arrested 12 December 2017, sentenced 3 September 2018 to seven years under Official Secrets Act for reporting on Inn Din massacre (2 September 2017). Police officer's entrapment testimony confirmed. Both released 7 May 2019 via presidential pardon. Year 2018 is accurate for sentencing.

title: Gambia Files ICJ Genocide Case Against Myanmar
note: Confirmed: Gambia filed case at ICJ on 11 November 2019 on behalf of OIC. ICJ issued provisional measures 23 January 2020 ordering Myanmar to protect Rohingya and preserve evidence. Case ongoing into 2026. Year and facts verified.

title: NLD Wins Second Landslide Election, Military Disputes Results
note: Confirmed: NLD won 396 of 476 contested seats in November 2020. Military and USDP immediately alleged voter fraud, rejected by Union Election Commission and international observers. Military coup followed on 1 February 2021. Year and facts verified.

title: Military Coup — Tatmadaw Seizes Power on February 1
note: Confirmed: Coup on 1 February 2021. Suu Kyi, President Win Myint, hundreds of elected officials arrested. Min Aung Hlaing declared year-long state of emergency, transferred authority to himself as SAC head. Parliament was to be sworn in that day. All core facts verified.

title: Civil Disobedience Movement and Mass Spring Revolution Protests
note: Confirmed: Nationwide CDM shut down government ministries, banks, hospitals, schools. Over 1,400 confirmed civilian deaths by end of 2021. Military deployed against protesters from February 2021. PDF formation accelerated. Year and facts verified.

title: People's Defence Force and National Unity Government Established
note: Confirmed: NUG established in April 2021 by deposed elected officials. PDF formed from former protesters trained by ethnic armed organizations. SAC designated NUG a terrorist organization. Decentralized insurgency across central Myanmar. Year and facts verified.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Sentenced to 27 Years in Secret Junta Trials
note: Confirmed: Suu Kyi's total sentence reached 33 years by 30 December 2022 after accumulating convictions through 2022. Later reduced to 27 years (reported April 2026). Trials held in secret at Naypyidaw Special Court, later moved inside Insein prison. Charges included corruption, COVID violations, Official Secrets Act. Year and facts verified (27-year figure reflects post-reduction sentence reported by Japan Times April 2026).

title: Junta Executes Four Democracy Activists — First Executions in Decades
note: Confirmed: Ko Jimmy (Kyaw Min Yu), Phyo Zeya Thaw, Hla Myo Aung, and Aung Thura Zaw executed on 25 July 2022 — Myanmar's first political executions in ~30 years. Military tribunal sentencing in January 2022 under Counterterrorism Law. UN, ASEAN, Western governments condemned. Year and facts verified.

title: Myanmar Economy Collapses Under Junta Rule
note: Confirmed: UN estimated 40% of Myanmar's population in poverty by 2022. Kyat lost over 60% of value. Banking system destabilized. Foreign investment fled. Healthcare and education systems deteriorated due to CDM. Year and scale of collapse verified.

title: Operation 1027 — Ethnic Forces Overrun Junta Positions in Shan State
note: Confirmed: Three Brotherhood Alliance (MNDAA, TNLA, Arakan Army) launched Operation 1027 on 27 October 2023. Over 220 junta positions captured in weeks. Unprecedented soldier surrenders and defections. Sparked allied operations in Rakhine, Chin, Karen, Sagaing. Year and facts verified.

title: Junta Conscription Law Triggers Mass Flight of Young People
note: Year error: The People's Military Service Law (conscription law) was enforced on 10 February 2024, not 2023. The law existed since 2010 but was only activated in February 2024. The mass exodus and fears were documented in February-March 2024. Event year should be 2024.

title: Arakan Army Captures Most of Rakhine State Including Bangladesh Border
note: Confirmed: Arakan Army launched Maungdaw offensive 21 May 2024; captured Maungdaw Township on 8 December 2024, gaining full control of 271km border with Bangladesh. Now controls 11 of 17 Rakhine State townships. Rohingya displacement between contending forces documented. Year and facts verified.

title: Humanitarian Crisis — Over 3 Million Internally Displaced
note: Confirmed: UN OCHA reported 3 million+ IDPs as of August 2024; rose to 3.5 million by end of 2024. Food insecurity acute across multiple regions. Humanitarian access constrained by junta obstruction. Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar (~1 million) an additional parallel crisis. Year and scale verified.

title: Myanmar Civil War Enters Fifth Year with No Settlement in Sight
note: Confirmed: Myanmar entered fifth year of military rule on 1 February 2025. SAC conducted elections in December 2025/January 2026 rather than outright postponing; however characterization of no credible settlement is accurate. Russian weapons, Chinese diplomatic cover, and resource revenue (jade, gems, gas) sustaining junta confirmed. Resistance gains continuing. Year and core characterization verified, though the event description overstates election cancellation — junta actually held a flawed election in late 2025.
